keyVerseText: The fountains also of the deep and the windows of heaven were stopped, and the rain from heaven was restrained;
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb כָּלָא (kâlâʼ) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys the idea of restriction or holding back. Its core sense involves actions such as shutting up, restraining, or withholding, which go beyond simple prohibition to include a physical or metaphorical confinement or cessation. This root meaning enriches the common English glosses by emphasizing not only forbidding but also the active containment or finishing of something, highlighting a comprehensive control over movement or flow.
usageInScripture: Throughout its 18 occurrences, כָּלָא consistently carries the sense of restraining or withholding, whether by physical confinement or by prohibitive action. Translations such as 'is stayed,' 'was restrained,' 'forbid,' and 'shut up' reveal a semantic range focused on limitation and cessation. This range shows the word's flexibility in describing both active and passive states of restriction, from divine intervention to human actions, underscoring its thematic consistency in Scripture.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding כָּלָא deepens our grasp of God's sovereign control over creation, as it signifies His ability to restrain and withhold according to His will. This verb highlights the divine prerogative to limit chaos and to bring order, reflecting God's power to finish His purposes and to protect His people by withholding what could harm them. For the Christian faith, it affirms that God is not only a creator but also a governor who actively restrains evil and disorder, pointing ultimately to Christ who holds all things together and restrains the enemy until the appointed time.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 8:2, the use of כָּלָא in the phrase 'the rain from heaven was restrained' vividly portrays God's sovereign action to stop the floodwaters by withholding their continual outpouring. This verb emphasizes the divine control over natural forces, marking a decisive moment when God halts judgment and begins restoration. The word conveys not just a pause but a deliberate and authoritative cessation, illustrating God's power to bring an end to chaos and to preserve life.
